newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African opposition accuses ANC of racism.
newsitem.headline: S.African opposition accuses ANC of racism.

text.p: South African opposition parties, including the creators of apartheid, accused President Nelson Mandela's ruling ANC of racism on Tuesday and said the country was slipping into decay.

Official leader of the opposition F.W. de Klerk, whose National Party introduced apartheid in 1948 and began dismantling it in 1990, made his attack in a parliamentary speech replying to Mandela's opening address last week.
"The African National Congress, despite its lip service to non-racialism and reconciliation, plays a hard game of racist politics and incites racist emotions whenever it suits itself," de Klerk said.
"I want to accuse the ANC today... that it is plunging the country into a form of new apartheid and that it is fomenting colour prejudices."
De Klerk was speaking on the seventh anniversary of Mandela's release from jail after serving 27 years of a life sentence imposed for treason against the apartheid state.
Mandela, opening parliament on Friday, made an impassioned plea for reconciliation and urged opposition parties to help the ANC make South Africa a better country.
De Klerk, noting the ANC had achieved some successes since sweeping him from power three years ago, said it was time for it to move from words to deeds, especially on economic issues.

"If the promised privatisation doesn't materialise on schedule, confidence will again be shaken. If no definite steps are taken soon with regard to the removal of exchange controls, confidence will wane...at the end will be growing poverty, failure in delivery and finally anarchy," he said.
Tony Leon, leader of the largely white liberal Democratic Party, echoed the charge that the ANC was now practising the racism against which it had fought as a liberation movement.

"I see a revolutionary movement, which stood for perhaps the greatest universal good in the 20th Century -- the eradication of racialism and the elimination of the scourge of apartheid, now practising a new racialism instead of the new patriotism," Len told parliament.

He cited verbal ANC attacks on critical journalists and the official policy of hiring people for their skin colour rather than merit as evidence that the ANC was "saddling up entitlement, resentment, envy and prejudice."
